isNonTraceabilityJSDocTagLine(normalized: string): - Detects any non-traceability JSDoc tag line: ```ts const trimmed = normalized.trimStart(); if (!trimmed || !trimmed.startsWith("@")) return false; if (/^@(story|req|supports)\b/.test(trimmed)) return false; return true; ``` - This matches any `@word` except @story/@req/@supports, fulfilling REQ-JSDOC-BOUNDARY-DETECTION and REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE. - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts - processCommentLine(...) imports normalizeCommentLine and isNonTraceabilityJSDocTagLine. - JSDoc coexistence logic: ```ts // Implement JSDoc tag coexistence behavior: terminate @story/@req values when a new non-traceability JSDoc tag line (e.g., @param, @returns) is encountered. // @supports docs/stories/022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE.story.md REQ-ANNOTATION-TERMINATION REQ-CONTINUATION-LOGIC if (isNonTraceabilityJSDocTagLine(normalized)) { finalizePendingAnnotation(context, comment, options, pending); return null; } ``` - Any non-traceability JSDoc tag line terminates the pending @story/@req value → REQ-ANNOTATION-TERMINATION, REQ-JSDOC-BOUNDARY-DETECTION. - Continuation logic: ```ts if (pending) { const continuation = normalized.trim(); if (!continuation) return pending; const updatedValue = pending.value ? `${pending.value} ${continuation}` : continuation; return { ...pending, value: updatedValue, hasValue: pending.hasValue || continuation.length > 0 }; } ``` - traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for Story 022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE are satisfied:
1) Before Other Tags / After Other Tags / Mixed Positions: - Covered by three explicit valid tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts (traceability before other tags, after other tags, and mixed with @param/@returns). All pass under Jest.
2) Proper Termination / JSDoc Tag Detection / Continuation Lines: - isNonTraceabilityJSDocTagLine treats any `@word` that is not @story/@req/@supports as a JSDoc boundary. - processCommentLine finalizes a pending @story/@req whenever such a boundary appears, then clears pending, so subsequent JSDoc lines are not concatenated to the traceability value. - Continuation logic only runs for lines that are not JSDoc-tag lines and only when a pending annotation exists. This matches REQ-ANNOTATION-TERMINATION, REQ-JSDOC-BOUNDARY-DETECTION, and REQ-CONTINUATION-LOGIC.
3) Error Messages / No False Positives: - The dedicated test reproducing the original bug (`[REQ-NO-FALSE-POSITIVES] JSDoc tags do not pollute requirement ID when following @req`) passes, demonstrating that valid annotations followed by JSDoc tags no longer generate spurious format errors. - Existing invalid-format tests (from story 005.0 and 010.*) still pass, showing that true format issues continue to produce clear, actionable error messages.
4) Preserve Multiline & Backward Compatibility: - Multi-line traceability values followed by JSDoc tags are validated by the `[REQ-PRESERVE-MULTILINE] multi-line @story annotation before other JSDoc tags` test, confirming that multiline values are preserved and terminated correctly at the first JSDoc tag line. - All previous tests for annotation validation and @supports multi-story behavior pass unmodified, indicating no regression and satisfying the backward compatibility requirement.
5) Documentation & Tests: - docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md explicitly documents JSDoc coexistence, tag boundaries, continuation behavior, and the resolved Issue #3 scenario, referencing this story file. - Tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts are annotated with @story docs/stories/022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE.story.md and cover all specified JSDoc combinations.
Given the concrete implementation, passing tests, and updated documentation, this story is fully implemented and passes.
